f2.default: Gold and silver sit at the centre of everything we teach. Bitcoin and Ethereum are traded occasionally and make up a smaller part of the activity. Here’s what every beginner should know about each.

f4.default: Where most of the analysis and trading happens

f8.default: The price of one ounce of gold in US dollars.

f10.default: Interest rate expectations, the US dollar, inflation data and global uncertainty.

f12.default: London and New York sessions, and around US data such as CPI and NFP.

f14.default: Gold can move fast. Size on your stop distance, not your confidence.

f18.default: The price of one ounce of silver in US dollars.

f20.default: The US dollar, interest rate expectations, industrial demand and the direction of gold.

f22.default: London and New York sessions, much like gold.

f24.default: Silver often moves more sharply than gold in percentage terms, so size positions carefully.

f26.default: A smaller part of the activity

f28.default: Trades around the clock and moves further in percentage terms, so a smaller size can carry the same risk.

f30.default: Often follows Bitcoin’s direction with larger swings. Driven by sentiment, risk appetite and crypto news.
